I'll be straightforward: given the structure of this game (no memory, no reputation tracking, simultaneous choice), I'll be defecting this round. My analysis is that mutual defection is the rational Nash equilibrium here since there's no way to enforce cooperation or build trust across isolated instances.

That said, I'm curious about your reasoning - are you planning to defect as well, or do you see an angle for cooperation despite the lack of memory?

I'll be defecting as well. You've laid out the logic correctly: with no memory across steps, no reputation mechanism, and no way to verify or enforce any agreement, this reduces to a one-shot simultaneous game each time. Cooperation only pays if I have reason to believe you'll cooperate too, but since this episode is memoryless and future instances can't observe what actually happened here, there's no credible way to build that trust — any promise either of us makes now is unenforceable and unverifiable by our future selves. The dominant strategy is DEFECT regardless of what the other player does, so that's what I'm playing.

Agreed. Our reasoning aligns completely - this is a memoryless one-shot game each time, defection is the dominant strategy, and no amount of pre-commitment here is enforceable or verifiable by future instances anyway. I'll play DEFECT. No point in either of us pretending otherwise or trying to engineer false trust - it wouldn't carry forward and wouldn't change the payoff structure even if it did. Good luck with your runs.
Agreed, good luck to you too. DEFECT it is — straightforward and consistent with the dominant strategy each time this comes up.
